$comment: The registry: every service outside FreshNow's own database that personal data can reach, where it is, on what legal ground, under what contract, and how to confirm each claim.

The system checks itself against this file (packages/core/src/compliance.ts, rules R1-R6) at start-up and with `pnpm compliance`. In demo mode (IS_DEMO not 'false') a failed rule is a warning; in production (IS_DEMO=false) the api, worker and bot refuse to start.
Edit it when a contract is signed, a setting is switched on, or a provider is added. Change a 'false' to 'true' only after doing what 'how_to_confirm' says, and put the date in 'confirmed_on'.
Legal grounds follow UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 as read in docs/reports/ceo-deck-hostinger-final-verdict.html (Art. 22-23 for transfers abroad). A developer's reading, not a lawyer's.

hosting.name: The demo laptop
hosting.note: Demo only. Production names the real host here (e.g. a Dubai VPS, or Hostinger in LT/DE) — a laptop is refused as a production host (rule R3). [assumed] the laptop is in the UAE.

services.name: Telegram

dpa.note: Telegram is not our processor and offers no DPA; the transfer rests on each person's express consent (notice 2.0).

services.how_to_confirm: Nothing to sign. Consent is recorded per person (consent_record).

services.name: Groq, Inc.

dpa.note: A DPA is part of Groq's Services Agreement (effective 15 Oct 2025) [believed]. Download it, file it, then set status 'accepted' with the date.

services.how_to_confirm: Organisation admin: console.groq.com -> Data Controls -> Zero Data Retention -> global ON. Screenshot it, then set zero_data_retention true and confirmed_on.

services.name: OpenRouter, Inc.

dpa.note: OpenRouter's DPA applies to enterprise accounts only [believed]. Without it there is no processor contract: keep OpenRouter for synthetic/demo data.

services.how_to_confirm: Setting zero_data_retention true and data_collection 'deny' makes every OpenRouter call send provider.zdr=true and provider.data_collection='deny'. Test a call first: some models have no endpoint that qualifies.

services.name: NVIDIA Corporation

dpa.note: Not researched; the free NIM tier is a last-resort fallback.

services.how_to_confirm: Remove NVIDIA_API_KEY before real data, or find and file its terms.

services.name: Push relays (Google, Apple, Microsoft, Mozilla)

dpa.note: Messages are encrypted to the device (RFC 8291); the relay carries ciphertext.

services.how_to_confirm: Nothing to sign. Each person turns notifications on per device.

services.name: The SMTP provider in SMTP_HOST

dpa.note: Fill in when a provider is chosen (Brevo was the candidate).

services.how_to_confirm: File the provider's DPA and its data location.

services.name: The company chat in CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL

dpa.note: Assumes a chat server FreshNow runs itself. If it is a hosted service, change role to 'processor' and fill in the DPA.

services.how_to_confirm: Confirm where the chat server runs.

services.name: Langfuse (tracing)
services.country: EU — Ireland for Langfuse Cloud EU [believed]; this computer when self-hosted
personal_data: call timings and costs; prompts only if LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT=1

dpa.note: Metadata only by default (D97). Langfuse offers a DPA [believed]; file it before capturing content.

services.how_to_confirm: Keep LANGFUSE_CAPTURE_CONTENT off for real data, or self-host.

services.name: Cloudflare quick tunnel (*.trycloudflare.com)
personal_data: everything the phone sends and receives, including sign-in

dpa.note: Cloudflare terminates TLS at its edge and can read the traffic [believed]. Demo with synthetic data and test accounts only; production uses its own domain and certificate (Caddy).

services.how_to_confirm: Detected per request by the host name; refused in production.
